# Spec: publish-commit
<!-- Generated by /hefesto:hef.spec -->
<!-- Date: 2026-11-06 -->
<!-- Board item: HEF-16 (deferred from HEF-14 / external-board plan review 2026-10-05, change 9) -->

## Overview

On an external board, `ledger.sh publish <id>` writes the state marker into a column file of the board
repo through `status-board.sh --mark`, and the person commits that edit. An opt-in
`orchestrate.publish_commit: true` makes `publish` commit the marked file itself — one path-limited
commit in the board repo, never pushed — behind five guards that keep it from sweeping a person's edits,
committing into a half-finished merge, writing outside the board repo, or losing a failed commit.

## Context (read from the code, 2026-11-06)

- `hooks/ledger.sh` `publish)` arm (lines ~797–836): for `tasks-repo` it hashes the item, calls
  `status-board.sh --mark <id> <marker> [--was <prev>]`, re-reads the item, re-records its hash with
  `ledger.sh record --body-file`, then writes `.published = {state, at}`.
- `hooks/status-board.sh` `mark_item()` (lines ~257–290) finds the column file under `$TROOT`, resolves a
  symlink with `readlink -f` and replaces the file via a temp file + `mv`; it prints
  `marked <id> <marker> in <column name>` — a column NAME, not a path.
- `hooks/board-lib.sh` `board_ctx` gives `mode` (`in-repo` | `external`) and `board_top` (the board repo's
  top, physical path); `is_external` tests the mode.
- `ledger.sh` is already over the 500-line file limit; new logic belongs in a sourced helper beside it
  (the pattern of `ledger-actions.sh`, `ledger-notes.sh`, `ledger-lifecycle.sh`).

## Decisions made here (no [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] needed)

- **D1 External boards only.** `publish_commit` applies when `ledger.sh board` reports `mode: external`
  and the entry's source is `tasks-repo`. On an in-repo board the column file lives in the code repo the
  person works in, where an automatic commit is exactly the sweep the item warns about: `publish` does not
  commit and says so in one line. A `github-project` source writes no file and is unaffected.
- **D2 Off unless exactly `true`.** Read as `.orchestrate.publish_commit // false` from the board config,
  like `orchestrate.publish`; it has effect only when `orchestrate.publish` is also `true`. Any other
  value (string `"true"`, number) is off.
- **D3 Branch expectation.** The commit lands on whatever branch the board repo's top currently has
  checked out — commonly `main`, since a board repo may take commits straight on main. `publish` never
  switches branch, never creates one, never pushes; pushing stays the person's. A detached HEAD is
  refused (a commit there is reachable from no branch). The output names the branch it committed on.
- **D4 A failed commit leaves nothing behind.** Because the file was verified clean before `--mark`, the
  only change in it is publish's own marker; on a failed commit `publish` restores that one path to its
  `HEAD` content, so the next pass finds it clean and retries from the start. Order is therefore
  mark → commit → re-hash → record `published` (today the re-hash follows the mark directly; moving it
  after the commit keeps the stored hash matching the board when the mark is rolled back).
- **D5 The commit runs under the project's neutral git config** (revised after plan review 2026-11-06,
  which found the first wording unimplementable). `ledger.sh` runs outside the lane sandbox and pins, for
  every git call it makes, the config keys that run a program (`hef_git_neutral`, `hooks/ledger.sh:268`,
  `hooks/lane-lib.sh:116`: `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, `core.fsmonitor=false`, …). The publish commit
  must not unset them: a board repo's hooks are NOT run (a lane able to write the board repo must not get
  a program executed unsandboxed). For the same reason the commit adds `commit.gpgsign=false` to that
  pinned set — `gpg.program` is a program-running key too — so a publish commit is unsigned; a board repo
  that requires signed commits leaves `publish_commit` off (documented). A failed commit is then a real
  git failure: no identity, an unwritable object store, a locked index (D4).
- **D8 One publish at a time per ledger.** D4's rollback is safe only if the column file holds nothing
  but this publish's marker; a lock (per ledger directory, shared by every repo the board feeds) spans
  locate → guards → mark → commit, so two publishes on the same column cannot sweep or roll back each
  other's marker.
- **D6 The commit is path-limited.** `git commit -- <abs path>` (a pathspec commit is git's `--only` mode), so anything else a
  person has staged in the board repo is neither committed nor unstaged.
- **D7 Fixed commit message.** `board: <id> <marker or "no marker">` — built only from the validated item
  id and the configured marker, never from item text (board text is untrusted data).

## User Scenarios

### US1: Publish commits the marked column on an external board [P1]
- **Given** an external board with `orchestrate.publish` and `orchestrate.publish_commit` both `true`, a
  clean board repo on branch `main`, and a ledger entry whose state changed
- **When** `ledger.sh publish <id>` runs from a code repo the board feeds
- **Then** the heading carries the new marker, the board repo has exactly one new commit on `main` whose
  only path is that column file and whose message is `board: <id> <marker>`, `published.state` is
  recorded, nothing is pushed, and the output names the branch
- **Edge:** the state is unchanged → no mark, no commit, `publish: unchanged` (as today)
- **Edge:** the item sits in DONE (`--mark` leaves it alone) → no commit, `published` recorded as today
- **Error / negative:** `publish_commit` absent or not exactly `true` → the file is marked and left
  uncommitted, byte-identical to today's behaviour

### US2: A dirty column file is refused before anything is written [P1]
- **Given** `publish_commit: true` and the column file that holds the item has uncommitted changes
  (unstaged, staged, or the file is untracked) in the board repo
- **When** `ledger.sh publish <id>` runs
- **Then** it exits non-zero naming the file and why, the file is byte-identical to before, no commit is
  made and `published` is not recorded
- **Edge:** a DIFFERENT file in the board repo is dirty or staged → allowed; the commit contains only the
  column file and the other file stays dirty/staged exactly as it was
- **Negative:** a person's edit in the column file must never appear in a publish commit

### US3: A merge, rebase or other sequencer state is refused [P1]
- **Given** `publish_commit: true` and the board repo has a merge, rebase (either backend), cherry-pick or
  revert in progress
- **When** `ledger.sh publish <id>` runs
- **Then** it exits non-zero naming the operation in progress; nothing is marked, committed or recorded
- **Edge:** detached HEAD (D3) → refused the same way, naming it

### US4: The column path comes from `--mark` and must be inside the board repo [P1]
- **Given** `publish_commit: true`
- **When** `status-board.sh --mark` rewrites a column file
- **Then** it reports the ABSOLUTE, symlink-resolved path of the file it rewrote, and `publish` commits
  that path — it never recomputes the path itself
- **And** before marking, `publish` resolves the same path (a locate step that writes nothing) and
  refuses when it is not inside the board repo's top — e.g. a column symlinked to another repository
- **Error / negative:** a column outside the board repo → non-zero, nothing written; no `git` command is
  ever run against a repository other than the board repo
- **Edge:** a column symlinked to another file INSIDE the board repo → allowed, the target is committed

### US5: A failed commit is retried, not lost [P1]
- **Given** `publish_commit: true`, all guards pass, and `git commit` fails (no user identity with
  `user.useConfigOnly`, an unwritable object store)
- **When** `ledger.sh publish <id>` runs
- **Then** it exits non-zero with git's reason, the column file is restored to its `HEAD` content,
  `published` and the stored body hash are unchanged, and the next `publish` with the cause fixed marks
  and commits normally
- **Negative:** `published` must never be recorded for a state whose commit did not happen

### US6: The branch expectation is stated [P2]
- **Given** a person enabling `publish_commit`
- **When** they read `docs/install.md` (external board section) and `docs/hooks.md` (`ledger.sh publish`)
- **Then** both say: external boards only, the commit lands on the board repo's checked-out branch (often
  `main`), path-limited, never pushed, unsigned and with the board repo's hooks not run (D5), the ledger
  process needs a git identity, and the refusals

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-001 | `ledger.sh publish` commits the marked column file in the board repo only when the board is external, the source is `tasks-repo`, and both `orchestrate.publish` and `orchestrate.publish_commit` are exactly `true`; otherwise behaviour is unchanged, and on an in-repo board with `publish_commit: true` one line says it was not committed (D1, D2). | P1 | US1 |
| FR-002 | Before `--mark`, `publish` refuses (non-zero, nothing written) when the item's column file has unstaged or staged changes or is untracked in the board repo; other paths do not block. | P1 | US2 |
| FR-003 | Before `--mark`, `publish` refuses when the board repo (the worktree at `board_top`) has a merge, rebase (merge or apply backend), cherry-pick or revert in progress, or HEAD is detached, naming which. | P1 | US3 |
| FR-004 | `status-board.sh --mark` reports the absolute, symlink-resolved path of the file it rewrote, and offers a write-nothing locate of the same path; `publish` refuses a path outside `board_top` before marking and commits exactly the path `--mark` reported. Existing `--mark` output consumers (`not marked` on DONE) keep working. | P1 | US4 |
| FR-005 | The commit is `git -C <board_top> commit -m "board: <id> <marker>" -- <abs path>` (a pathspec commit, git's `--only` mode): one path, under the neutral git config plus `commit.gpgsign=false`, never unsetting a pinned key, no push, no branch change (D3, D5, D6, D7). | P1 | US1 |
| FR-006 | Order is mark → commit → re-hash → record `published`. On a failed commit, the column path is restored to its `HEAD` content, the error names git's reason, and neither the body hash nor `published` is written, so the next pass retries. A per-ledger lock spans locate → commit (D8). | P1 | US5 |
| FR-007 | The success line names the branch committed on (`… committed on <branch>, not pushed`). | P2 | US1, US6 |
| FR-008 | `docs/install.md` and `docs/hooks.md` document `orchestrate.publish_commit`: external only, branch expectation, path-limited, never pushed, unsigned with hooks not run, a git identity required, the refusals; `CHANGELOG.md` gets an Unreleased entry. | P2 | US6 |
| FR-009 | The new logic lives in a sourced helper beside `ledger.sh` (it is over the file limit), failing loudly per constitution 5: every refusal exits non-zero with the offending path or state. | P2 | all |

## Success Criteria

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | On the existing external fixture (`tests/smoke.sh`, `eb_*`), publish with `publish_commit: true` adds exactly one commit on the board repo's branch touching only the column file, with the fixed message, and records `published`. | smoke assertion on `git log -1 --name-only` and the ledger entry |
| SC-002 | Each refusal (dirty column, staged column, untracked column, merge, rebase, cherry-pick, detached HEAD, column outside the board repo) leaves the column file byte-identical, no new commit, `published` unchanged. | one smoke assertion per refusal, comparing sha256 and `HEAD` |
| SC-003 | A commit with no identity (`user.useConfigOnly=true`, no `user.email`, global/system config off) → non-zero, file restored to HEAD, body hash and `published` unchanged; with the identity restored the next publish commits. A `pre-commit` hook in the board repo that would fail is NOT run (the commit succeeds). | smoke assertion |
| SC-004 | With `publish_commit` off, absent or `"true"` (string), publish output and board state match today's test exactly; the existing FR-006 external-board assertions stay green. | existing + one new smoke assertion |
| SC-005 | Every guard is mutation-tested (constitution 3): disabling each of the dirty check, the sequencer check, the in-repo path check, the commit-before-record order, the rollback, the lock, and the `-- <path>` pathspec turns the suite red. | mutation list in the plan, run during `/hefesto:hef.verify` |
| SC-006 | `tests/smoke.sh` tier 1 and `node --test` pass; `bash -n` / shellcheck clean on touched hooks; macOS static guard passes (no GNU-only flags). | CI-equivalent local run |

- `hooks/ledger.sh` — `publish)` arm: call the helper, reorder re-hash after commit
- `hooks/ledger-publish.sh` (new, sourced) — guards, commit, rollback
- `hooks/status-board.sh` + a sourced `hooks/board-mark.sh` — `--mark` reports the absolute path; a locate mode
- `tests/smoke.sh` — the external-board publish block
- `docs/hooks.md`, `docs/install.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

## Clarifications

_None — every open point was decidable from the code and the item; decisions are D1–D8 above._
D5 was revised after the plan review (2026-11-06): its first wording ("honour hooks and signing")
contradicted the repository's own security invariant (`hef_git_neutral`); the invariant wins.
